paper.one_line_finding: Among 844 online volunteers analyzed (3,414 AUT ideas analyzed), seeing ChatGPT example ideas did not change classifier-scored originality (joint F(4, 19.86) = 0.12, p = 0.97; p. 8, Section 5.4; per-arm coefficients in Table 18, p. 26), but both high-exposure conditions raised global idea diversity over the human-examples control (Cliff's delta 0.31 disclosed and 0.26 undisclosed, adjusted p = 0.001; p. 7, Section 5.2; Table 12, p. 22).
paper.shared_samples: None for the S1 participants. The S1 seed examples and the S2 human ideas come from the Organisciak et al. AUT dataset; those people are not S1 participants.

studies.label: Dynamic online Alternate Uses Task experiment: AI exposure and disclosure
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Assignment is to randomized within-person condition/item sequences, not to randomized clusters. Local-outcome mixed models include participant random intercepts crossed with response chains nested in item-condition combinations (PDF p. 14, Appendix B.1). Global diversity uses permutation tests paired on item and Monte Carlo seed (PDF p. 21, SI 8.1); diversity evolution uses item random intercepts on pooled idea sets (PDF p. 25, SI 8.3). The latter analyses do not supply participant-level uncertainty.

estimates.outcome: Global idea diversity: median pairwise cosine distance
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: SBERT embeddings; median pairwise cosine distance, multiplied by 100 by the authors. For each condition-item combination, 50 ideas are sampled in each of 50 Monte Carlo runs, using submitted ideas after the sixth trial of a response chain. Contrasts compare means of the resulting set-level diversity values, paired on item and Monte Carlo seed (PDF p. 21, SI 8.1). The exact SBERT checkpoint is not named.

stats.difference_is: As printed in Diff in Means: treatment minus control, in the authors' scaled cosine-distance units.

paper_effect.standardizer: Nonparametric ordering effect across Monte Carlo set-diversity values; no SD standardizer. Positive means larger diversity in the first named condition (PDF p. 21, SI 8.1).

open_items: The number randomized, per-arm participant counts, complete-pair counts and distinct participant counts for each analysis are not printed. The study-wide analyzed count is not substituted for any unknown analysis count.

No first-round-only comparison is reported. Retained records use the randomized within-person sequence, with incomplete sequences and possible carryover into later Control trials. The paired code describes use of repeated-condition data, not complete pairing or a paired t test.

Individual-originality arm means, participant-level SDs, outcome SDs and standardized treatment effects are not printed. Regression intercepts and coefficient SEs cannot replace arm means or outcome SDs.

Global-diversity arm levels and confidence limits appear only graphically for the main metric. No figure values were read off. Tables 11-13 supply differences, adjusted permutation p-values and Cliff's deltas, but no numerical arm levels or effect SEs and confidence limits.

Global-diversity inference uses Monte Carlo/item pairs; evolution inference uses pooled idea sets with item random intercepts. Neither supplies uncertainty that accounts for the randomized participants.

Table 17 prints Control trial-number slopes and treatment-minus-Control slope differences, but no arm means or numerical AI-arm slopes and their uncertainty. Control slopes and coefficient SEs are preserved in resolutions. Means, mean SEs and unprinted AI slopes are not calculated or substituted.

PDF p. 8, Section 5.2 assigns the positive low-exposure global-diversity result to Undisclosed, whereas PDF p. 22, Table 12 assigns it to Disclosed and gives a negative result for Undisclosed. Extraction follows the explicit table rows; this textual inconsistency remains unresolved.

The abstract says there were no main effects of disclosure, whereas the global-diversity tables print significant disclosure contrasts. Table values are retained without resolving the authors' interpretation.

Full-sample marginal pairwise contrasts are not printed for local idea distance or AI adoption. Condition coefficients in Tables 14 and 22 are conditional on person moderators; centering is not stated. Local distance and AI adoption remain eligible output-based outcomes, but their conditional/moderation results are excluded.

The difference between retained responses in SI 3 and model observation counts is not explained. The observation count for each entire model is recorded as n_units and explicitly distinguished from people and from a two-arm observation count.

The landing page tells everyone examples may come from AI (PDF p. 5, Figure 3). Undisclosed omits source labels, despite the broader description on PDF p. 4 saying participants were not told ideas came from AI.

Table 1 calls AI adoption maximum semantic distance, whereas Sections 1.2.2 and 5.5 and SI 10 define it as maximum cosine similarity. Local idea distance is in SI 8.2, despite Table 1's reference to SI 8.3. The defining sections and model captions determine the outcome descriptions.
The SBERT checkpoint and ChatGPT-3.5 release year are not stated; no release year is inferred from implementation dates. No preregistration was identified in the complete supplied document.
